LESSON: GRAMMAR IN USE 3.3.1 LANGUAGE PATTERN

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 3
Topic 3.3: Grammar in Use 3.3.1 Language pattern

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Grammar in Use 3.3.1 Language pattern. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why should we use correct sentences in our speech or writing?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. use the target language pattern in sentences correctly for fluency in speech
2. respond to questions on the language patterns in written communication

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: GRAMMAR IN USE 3.3.1 LANGUAGE PATTERN
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE · Grade: Grade 4
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Grammar in Use 3.3.1 Language pattern helps you succeed in ENGLISH LANGUAGE. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: GRAMMAR IN USE 3.3.1 LANGUAGE PATTERN
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Use the target language pattern in sentences correctly for fluency in speech

What this means
In this part you learn to use the target language pattern in sentences correctly for fluency in speech. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: use the target language pattern in sentences correctly for fluency in speech.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Grammar in Use 3.3.1 Language pattern”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can use the target language pattern in sentences correctly for fluency in speech. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Respond to questions on the language patterns in written communication

What this means
In this part you learn to respond to questions on the language patterns in written communication. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: respond to questions on the language patterns in written communication.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Grammar in Use 3.3.1 Language pattern to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can respond to questions on the language patterns in written communication. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Grammar in Use 3.3.1 Language pattern is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Grammar in Use 3.3.1 Language pattern”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: use the target language pattern in sentences correctly for fluency in speech)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Grammar in Use 3.3.1 Language pattern to a partner. (skill: respond to questions on the language patterns in written communication)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Grammar in Use 3.3.1 Language pattern to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: use the target language pattern in sentences correctly for fluency in speech.
3. Practise this skill: respond to questions on the language patterns in written communication.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Grammar in Use 3.3.1 Language pattern from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Grammar in Use 3.3.1 Language pattern: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 4 learner study Grammar in Use 3.3.1 Language pattern?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why should we use correct sentences in our speech or writing?
2. How can we write sentences correctly?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Grammar in Use 3.3.1 Language pattern means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: use the target language pattern in sentences correctly for fluency in speech.
5. Be able to: respond to questions on the language patterns in written communication.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
